verdict.rationale: Stripe documents machine payments over MPP and x402 where the server returns an HTTP 402 challenge. The agent pays and retries without a checkout UI, and Stripe settles to the seller's balance, with per-call pricing, an agent build prompt and the `mppx validate` conformance tool; a probe confirms the mppx SDK and the open spec are published. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of an end-to-end paid call (a community note calls the end-to-end docs sparse), plus a 0.50 USD card minimum that constrains micro-priced calls on the SPT rail.

support.subject: As a developer, I can monetize an API or service with HTTP 402 machine payments that agents pay per call without a checkout UI

citations.quote: is an open protocol that lets agents pay for your APIs and services programmatically without a checkout UI, co-authored by Stripe and Tempo
When an agent requests your API or service, your server returns an HTTP `402` response with payment details.
Your server returns a payment challenge, the agent presents a valid payment credential, and Stripe settles the payment to your Stripe balance.
When a client requests a paid resource, your server returns an HTTP 402 response with payment details, including a Stripe deposit address.
